about_accessibility_text: This UI is extremely useful for building business-style applications that need a consistent, polished look and feel — and its accessibility features are top notch, which is a must for any business application.
about_disclaimer_text: FluentUI Svelte is an independent, community-built project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Microsoft in any way. Fluent UI and its design language are trademarks of Microsoft; this library is simply an implementation of that design system for Svelte.
about_help_text: FluentUI Svelte has grown into a pretty large library — dozens of components, docs, examples, translations — and keeping up with all of it on my own, in my free time, is a real challenge. If you like this project and want to contribute, whether that's code, documentation, translations, or just reporting bugs, it would help a lot. Check out the open issues on GitHub, or take a look at the contributing guide to see where to start.
about_help_title: Looking for help maintaining this project
about_hero_image_alt: Placeholder hero image — replace with a real screenshot
about_intro_after_bold: FluentUI Svelte was created to provide a set of Svelte components that follow the Fluent UI design system for another personal project.
about_intro_bold: Firstly, thank you for checking out this project!
about_journey_text: Publishing this library publicly took me more than a year. I work full-time, and I also maintain other personal projects that take up a good chunk of my free time, so progress on FluentUI Svelte wasn't always fast. Ironically, it was using this library extensively in those very projects that gave me the confidence to finally open it up — seeing it hold up in real, day-to-day applications convinced me it was ready for other people to use too.
about_journey_title: Why it took over a year to go public
about_paragraph3: I'll keep improving this package whenever I can. If you'd like to support the project, a star or a donation through GitHub Sponsors goes a long way — and it's genuinely appreciated!
about_showcase_image_alt: Placeholder showcase image — replace with real app screenshots
about_tauri_text: FluentUI Svelte has also been used to build full desktop applications with Tauri, running just as well on Windows, macOS, and Linux. The combination of Rust, Svelte, and Tauri is brutally fast, gives you granular control over every detail, and reactivity that feels top-tier. And because the visual style follows Windows' own design language, it feels familiar to almost anyone — most people have used Windows at some point, so without even realizing it, they already know how to use an interface built with Fluent UI.
about_tauri_title: From desktop to any OS, thanks to Tauri
about_tech_text1: I chose Svelte over Fluent UI's official Web Components for a few concrete reasons. First, performance: Svelte is consistently ranked among the fastest frameworks out there, since it compiles components into optimized JavaScript instead of shipping a heavy runtime. Second, Svelte's developer experience and reactivity are on another level. And third, the Shadow DOM used by the official Web Components is a real headache for anyone who needs to customize styles or integrate them with another library.
about_tech_text2: For the same reason, I went with plain CSS instead of Tailwind: in large, enterprise applications, migrating from Tailwind 3 to 4 (or across any major version) can be a huge undertaking. CSS, on the other hand, will always just be CSS, no matter how many updates come along — it's the safer long-term bet for a library other people are going to build on top of.
about_tech_title: Technical decisions: why Svelte and plain CSS
about_ux_text: I don't have formal reviews to point to, but there's one thing I keep hearing from people using apps built with this UI: they just get it. Because everything follows a consistent, familiar design system, users pick up how to navigate the interface almost immediately, with very little learning curve.
about_ux_title: What people notice when using it
asb_description: The AutoSuggestBox component provides an input field with dynamic suggestions as users type. It enhances user experience by offering relevant suggestions, improving efficiency in form inputs and searches.
asb_keyboard_navigation_description: Users can navigate through suggestions using the Up and Down arrow keys. Pressing Enter selects the highlighted suggestion.
asb_suggestions_description: Suggestions are provided as {#code}AutoSuggestBoxOption{/code} a children of the {#code}AutoSuggestBox{/code}. As the user types, matching options will be shown.
avatar_badge_description: An avatar can have a badge to indicate presence status. See the PresenceBadge component for more info.
avatar_colorful_description: An avatar can have its color automatically picked based on the name prop, or idForColor can be used if a name is not available.
avatar_description: An Avatar is a graphical representation of a user, team, or entity.
avatar_icon_description: An avatar can display an icon. The icon will only be shown when there is no image or initials available.
avatar_image_description: An avatar can display an image. It is recommended to also include a name in addition to the image: the initials from the name are displayed while the image is loading, and the name makes the Avatar accessible to screen readers.
avatar_overview_description: Avatar can display an image, icon, or initials, and supports different sizes, shapes, and status indicators.
avatar_shape_description: An avatar can have a square, circular, or rounded shape.
badge_appearance_description: Use the appearance prop to switch between filled, outline, tint, and ghost styles.
badge_badgeicon_api_description: This component is useful when you want to show an icon in the form of a Badge somewhere in your app.

badge_color_description: Use the color prop to communicate different statuses and priorities.
badge_description: A badge is a visual decoration for UI elements used to display notifications, status indicators, or counts. It supports different colors and styles to match various UI needs.
badge_icon_description: Use the icon prop to render an icon inside the badge. You can pass the icon as a snippet or as a component.
badge_only_icon_description: If you use this component and notice padding between the wrapper and the icon, use the BadgeIcon component instead to avoid it.
badge_shapes_description: Use the shape prop to render circular, rounded, or square badges.
badge_sizes_description: Use the size prop to control the badge dimensions.
btn_adding_a_menu_description_after_link: for details on how to create menus and pass them as a prop to the SplitButton component.
btn_adding_a_menu_description_before_lin: To add a menu to the split button, please refer to the
btn_appearance_description: A button can have its content and borders styled for greater emphasis or to be subtle.
btn_description: A button triggers an action or event when activated and supports three visual appearances: accent, standard, and subtle.
btn_shape_description: A button can be rounded, circular, or square. Default: rounded.
btn_split_button_description: A split button is a special type of button that combines a standard button with a menu button to provide users with a primary action and additional options.
cb_description: Represents a control that a user can select (check) or clear (uncheck). A CheckBox can also report its value as indeterminate.
cb_disabled_description: The `disabled` prop disables the checkbox, preventing user interaction. It accepts a boolean value.
cb_indeterminate_description: The `indeterminate` prop sets the checkbox to an indeterminate state, which is useful for representing a mixed selection.
cb_label_description: To display a visible label, set `wrapperAs="label"` and pass the label text as children. The wrapper then renders as a `<label>` element that wraps the input.
cdp_component_api_description: The Calendar Date Picker builds on Calendar View, so calendar props such as blackoutDates, minDate, maxDate, weekStart and headers are forwarded straight to the popup calendar. You can see the full list in the Component Props section below.
cdp_description: The Calendar Date Picker pairs a button trigger with a Calendar View popup. Clicking the trigger opens the calendar, and selecting a day updates the bound value and closes the popup.
cv_description: The Calendar View is an inline calendar for browsing days, months and years. It supports selecting a single date or several dates, minimum and maximum bounds, blackout dates, and a configurable week start and locale.
cv_multiple_description: Set the multiple prop to allow selecting more than one date.
cv_range_description: Set selectionMode to range to pick a start and an end. The range has its own binding rather than sharing value, and end stays null between the two clicks, so a half-built range is distinguishable from a range of a single day.
cv_week_start_description: Use the weekStart prop to change the first day of the week (0 = Sunday, 3 = Wednesday).
dd_custom_option_description: Options can render any content, such as a Persona. Pass a text prop so the closed dropdown can still display the selection.
dd_description: The Dropdown lets users select one or more options from a list of DropdownOption children. Options can render rich content, such as a Persona, and the current selection is exposed through a bindable value.
dd_multiple_description: Set the multiple prop to allow selecting more than one option at a time while pressing Ctrl (or Cmd on Mac).
dialog_composition_description: The Dialog is composed of several components that work together through a shared context:
dialog_composition_dialog_description: The root component that creates the state and provides context to its children.
dialog_composition_dialogactions_descrip: The footer that holds action buttons.
dialog_composition_dialogcontent_descrip: The scrollable body of the dialog.
dialog_composition_dialogsurface_descrip: The `<dialog>` element that hosts the dialog content.
dialog_composition_dialogtitle_descripti: The heading of the dialog. Renders as an `h3` by default.
dialog_composition_dialogtrigger_descrip: A button that opens the dialog when clicked.
dialog_description: A dialog is a window overlaid on either the primary window or another dialog window.
dialog_with_actions_description: Add a DialogActions region to render action buttons in the dialog footer. Use bind:this on the Dialog to call closeDialog() programmatically.
divider_align_content_description: The `alignContent` prop controls where the label content (children) is positioned along the divider. Possible values: `'start'`, `'center'`, `'end'`.
divider_align_content_vertical_descripti: It also works combined with the `vertical` prop:
divider_appearance_description: Controls the color of the divider. Possible values: `'standard'`, `'accent'`, `'subtle'`.
divider_custom_element_description: The `as` prop lets you change the underlying HTML element rendered by the divider. Possible values: `'div'`, `'hr'`, `'span'`.
divider_description: The Divider component is used to visually separate content within a layout. It can be oriented horizontally or vertically.
divider_inset_description: When `inset` is set, the divider gets some inline padding applied, useful when it's placed inside a container that has content touching its edges.
divider_vertical_description: When `vertical` is set, the divider renders on the vertical axis instead of the horizontal one. Make sure the parent container has a defined height so the divider is visible.
docs_overview_attention_description: This package isn't a exact re-implementation of Fluent UI, many features are not exactly as described in the FluentUI Documentation.
docs_overview_description: Welcome to the FluentUI Svelte documentation! This page will explain the basic concepts of the library.
dp_description: The Date Picker lets users select a date from carousel-style day, month and year columns. Its value uses the YYYY-MM-DD format, and any column can be hidden to build, for example, a month and year only picker.
dp_format_description: Use the format prop to switch between dd/MM/yyyy and MM/dd/yyyy.
dp_hiding_columns_description: Use hideDays, hideMonths or hideYears to hide individual selector columns, for example to build a month and year only picker.
ds_custom_option_description: Options can render rich content such as a Persona. Provide a text prop for the plain-text selection label.
ds_description: The Dropdown Select is a dropdown built on the native select element. It lets users choose one option, or several with the multiple prop, from a list of DropdownSelectOption children.
ds_multiple_description: Set the multiple prop to allow selecting more than one option at a time.
expander_adding_an_icon_description: You can easily add an icon to an expander’s header using the `Icon` prop. You can pass either a Snippet or a Component.
expander_controlling_expansion_descripti: Expanders can be either expanded or collapsed. This can be controlled by setting the `expanded` property.
expander_description: Control that displays a header and a collapsible content area.
expander_opening_direction_description: An expander doesn’t have to expand downwards. You can control an expander’s expansion direction using the `direction` property. To create an upwards-expanding expander, set `direction` to `up`.
expander_usage_description: A basic expander expects a header and its content. You can configure the header by passing the `header` property. Content can be provided as child elements of the component. By default, the content container has no padding, this allows you to use 100% of the content width if needed.
flyout_description: The Flyout component is a floating panel that can be used to display additional information or options in a non-intrusive way. It is fully accessible and follows Fluent UI design principles for a seamless user experience.
flyout_round_corners_description: Use the roundCorners prop to control which corners of the flyout are rounded. It accepts 'all', 'top', 'bottom', 'left' or 'right'.
flyout_usage_description: A flyout renders a floating surface around its content. On its own it is a static panel; set the floating prop and pass a reference element to have Floating UI position it against another element.

ib_description: The InfoBar control is for displaying app-wide status messages to users that are highly visible yet non-intrusive. There are built-in severity levels to easily indicate the type of message shown, as well as the option to include your own call to action or hyperlink button. Since the InfoBar is inline with other UI content, it can remain visible or be dismissed by the user.
ib_hide_close_button_description: The hideCloseButton prop allows you to hide the close button in the InfoBar.
ib_status_description: The status prop determines the visual style and meaning of the InfoBar.
ib_style_description: The style prop determines the layout of the InfoBar.
label_description: A Label provides an accessible caption for a form control. It supports different sizes and weights, can be marked as required or disabled, and can be positioned relative to the control it wraps.
label_position_description: Use the labelPosition prop to place the label text relative to the wrapped control. Possible values: 'before', 'after', 'above', 'below'.
label_required_description: Pass a required object to mark the label as required and render a required indicator, which defaults to an asterisk.
label_size_description: Use the size prop to control the label text size. Possible values: 'small', 'medium', 'large'.
label_weight_description: Use the weight prop to switch between a regular and a semibold label.

lv_description: The ListView is a component for rendering a set of vertically stacked items. These items can be focusable, selectable, have one primary action and one or more secondary actions, and support keyboard navigation and accessibility features.
lv_listviewitem_checkmark_description_pr: Add and configure a checkbox for the element. You can use the same props for the
lv_navigation_mode_description: This option allows you to set keyboard navigation based on your needs. For view-only data, you do not need to set this unless the items perform some action. If your items have multiple actionable elements within the ListViewItem, like buttons or menus, you can set this to composite.

menu_component_contextmenutrigger_descri: A variant of MenuTrigger that is designed to be used for context menus. It attaches the menu to a specified element and opens on right-click.
menu_component_menu_description: The root component that creates all the state and provides context to its children.
menu_component_menudivider_description: A visual separator between menu items or groups.
menu_component_menugroup_description: A wrapper for grouping related menu items together, with an optional header.
menu_component_menuitem_description: Represents a single item in the menu. It can be a simple action or a trigger for a nested menu.
menu_component_menuitemcheckbox_descript: A menu item that can be checked or unchecked.
menu_component_menuitemradio_description: A menu item that can be selected as part of a group of radio items.
menu_component_menuitemswitch_descriptio: A menu item that can be toggled on or off.
menu_component_menulist_description: A wrapper for the list of menu items.
menu_component_menupopover_description: The container for the menu content. It handles the positioning and accessibility of the menu.
menu_component_menutrigger_description: Handles all the logic for the trigger element that opens the menu. It uses a render prop pattern to provide the necessary props and state to the trigger element.

menu_description: Menu is a component for displaying a list of actions or options in a dropdown format. It can be used in various contexts, such as navigation, settings, or context menus.
menu_floating_ui_description_suffix: library for positioning. It provides a flexible API for creating complex menu structures, including nested menus, checkable items, and disabled items.
menu_optional_components_description: Other components that can be used within the menu include:

nb_description: The NumberBox component allows users to input numeric values with specified constraints such as minimum, maximum, and step values.
nb_variant_description: The variant prop determines the visual style of the NumberBox.
pbar_description: A progress bar is a horizontal indicator that communicates the progress of an operation. Set value for determinate progress, or omit it for an indeterminate animation when the duration is unknown.
pbar_hide_rail_description: The hideRail prop can be used to hide the progress bar rail.
pbar_indeterminate_description: If you do not set the value prop, the progress bar enters an indeterminate state, meaning it does not have a specific value. This is useful for operations where the duration is unknown.
pbar_status_description: The status prop allows you to set the status of the progress bar to 'paused' or 'error'. This changes the color of the progress bar to indicate different states.
pbar_value_description: The value prop sets the current progress value of the bar. It should be a number between 0 and 100.
persona_avatar_description: A Persona wraps an avatar inside it, which can be customized with all the props available to the Avatar component.
persona_description: A Persona is a visual representation of a person. It wraps an Avatar together with presence information and up to four lines of text: the name plus primary, secondary and tertiary text.
persona_presence_description: A Persona can display presence information, such as online status or availability. This is controlled through the presence prop, which accepts an object with a status key.
persona_size_description: A Persona supports custom sizes, with a default of 42px. You can set the size using the size prop. This applies to both the avatar or presence-only display and all text.
persona_text_align_description: A Persona supports three text alignments, with 'left' as the default position.
persona_text_position_description: A Persona supports four text positions: 'top', 'bottom', 'left', and 'right'. The default position is 'right'.
pring_description: A progress ring is a circular indicator that communicates the progress of an operation. Set value for determinate progress, or use indeterminate when the duration is unknown.
pring_hide_rail_description: The hideRail prop allows the progress ring to hide the rail, which is a background track for the progress indicator.
pring_indeterminate_description: The indeterminate prop allows the progress ring to display an indeterminate state, which is useful when the progress cannot be determined.
pring_status_description: The status prop allows you to set the status of the progress ring for visual feedback. It accepts values such as 'paused' or 'error'.
pring_value_description: The value prop determines the percentage of the progress ring that is filled. It should be a number between 0 and 100.
rb_checked_description: The checked prop allows you to control the checked state of the radio button. This is useful for controlled components.
rb_description: A radio button lets someone choose a single option from a set of mutually exclusive choices. Group several radio buttons with a shared name, or use bind:group to bind the selected value to a variable.
rb_disabled_description: The disabled prop can be used to disable a radio button, preventing user interaction.
rb_grouping_description: While you can use name="inputName" to group items and have only one checked, you can use bind:group to update that variable with the value of the selected input and inspect it in your console.
skeleton_animation_description: The `animation` prop controls which type of animation is used for the skeleton. It can be set to `pulse` or `wave`. The default is `wave`.
skeleton_description: The skeleton component provides a placeholder for content that is loading, giving users a visual indication of where content will appear once it has loaded.
skeleton_justify_description: Control if the skeleton should take the full width of its container or not. The default is `false`, meaning it will only take the `1:1` ratio of its width.
skeleton_shape_description: The `shape` prop allows you to change the shape of the skeleton. It can be set to `circle`, `square`, or `rounded`. The default is `rounded`.
skeleton_usage_description: The skeleton renders a placeholder element and sizes itself via standard HTML/CSS. Use the `style`, `class`, `width` and `height` attributes (or the `justify` prop) to control its dimensions.
slider_description: A slider lets users select a value from a continuous or discrete range by dragging a thumb along a track. It supports horizontal and vertical orientations, tick marks, a value tooltip and reverse direction.
slider_disabled_description: Set the disabled prop to prevent interaction with the slider.
slider_orientation_description: Set orientation to vertical to lay the slider out vertically. Make sure the container has a defined height so the slider is visible.
slider_range_description: Use the min, max and step props to control the range of values and the increment between them.
slider_ticks_description: Provide an array of values to the ticks prop to render tick marks along the track. Use tickPlacement to position them around, before or after the rail.
ta_description: Textarea allows the user to enter and edit multiline text.
ta_on_change_description: The `onChange` event is triggered whenever the content of the textarea changes. This can be used to react to user input in real-time, such as validating input or updating other parts of the UI.
ta_placeholder_description: The `placeholder` prop sets the placeholder text for the textarea, providing a hint to users about what to enter.
ta_resize_description: The `resize` prop controls whether the textarea can be resized by the user. It can be set to `none`, `both`, `horizontal`, or `vertical`. This allows you to control the resizing behavior of the textarea.
tb_description: The TextBox control lets a user type text into an app. It's typically used to capture a single line of text, but can be configured to capture multiple lines of text. The text displays on the screen in a simple, uniform, plaintext format.
tb_hide_buttons_description: The `hideActionButtons` prop allows you to hide the extra action buttons in the input, such as clear or submit buttons. This can be useful for a cleaner UI when those actions are not needed.
tb_readonly_description: The `readonly` prop makes the input field read-only, preventing users from modifying its value. This is useful for displaying information that should not be edited.
tb_type_description: The `type` prop specifies the type of input element. It can be set to various types such as `text`, `search`, `email`, `url`, `tel`, `password`, or `number`. This determines the behavior and validation of the input.
tooltip_component_api_description: A brief explanation of the props that really need explaining. You can see the rest of the props in the Component Props section below.
tooltip_delay_description: The openDelay and hideDelay props allow you to specify a delay, in milliseconds, before the tooltip is shown or hidden after the user hovers over the target element. This can help prevent the tooltip from appearing or disappearing too quickly.
tooltip_description: A tooltip displays additional information about another component. The information is displayed above and near the target component.
tooltip_usage_plain_description: You can also pass the target directly as a child. The tooltip then attaches itself to the next rendered element, but the accessibility attributes are not applied.
tooltip_usage_snippet_description: Use a children snippet to receive the tooltip's accessibility attributes and spread them onto the target element. The snippet also receives an attachment as its second argument, which you can attach to the element that should act as the trigger.
tooltip_with_arrow_description: The withArrow prop is a boolean that, when set to true, adds an arrow to the tooltip pointing towards the target element. This can help visually connect the tooltip to the element it is describing.
tp_description: The Time Picker lets users select a time from carousel-style hour, minute and second columns. It supports a 24-hour clock or a 12-hour clock with an AM/PM column, and any column can be hidden individually.
tp_format_description: Use the format prop to choose between a 24-hour clock and a 12-hour clock with an AM/PM column.
tp_hiding_columns_description: Use hideHours, hideMinutes or hideSeconds to hide individual columns. By default the seconds column is shown.
tswitch_description: A toggle switch represents a physical switch that allows someone to choose between two mutually exclusive options. For example, 'On/Off' and 'Show/Hide'. Choosing an option should produce an immediate result.
tswitch_states_description: A toggle switch can be labeled, checked or disabled.
tv_description: The Tree View displays hierarchical data in a nested list where each item can be expanded, checked or selected. Items are composed with the TreeViewItem and TreeViewItemContent components — the tree does not accept a data prop.
tv_usage_description: Nesting a TreeView inside a TreeViewItem of type='branch' creates a subtree. Use openItems / checkedItems on the root TreeView (bindable) to control open and checked state programmatically.
